statement: A circular fountain has a radius of $8$ feet. A straight garden path touches the edge of the fountain at exactly one point, $T$. A lamp stands on the path $15$ feet from $T$. What is the shortest distance, in feet, from the lamp to the edge of the fountain?

choices.misconception: I subtracted the radius from the distance along the path, $15 - 8 = 7$, but the shortest route to the edge points toward the center, not along the path.
I found the distance from the lamp to the center of the fountain, $17$ feet, and forgot to subtract the radius.
I found the distance to the center, $17$ feet, then added the radius, which gives the farthest point on the edge, not the nearest one.

hints: A radius drawn to the point of tangency is perpendicular to the tangent line.
The center, $T$ and the lamp form a right triangle with legs $8$ and $15$. The nearest point on the edge lies on the segment from the lamp to the center.
The lamp is $\sqrt{8^2 + 15^2} = 17$ feet from the center of the fountain.

solutions.reliable: The path is tangent to the circle at $T$, so the radius to $T$ is perpendicular to the path. The center $O$, the point $T$ and the lamp $L$ form a right triangle with legs $OT = 8$ and $TL = 15$, so $OL = \sqrt{64 + 225} = 17$ feet. The nearest point of the edge lies on $\overline{OL}$, one radius from $O$, so the shortest distance is $17 - 8 = 9$ feet.

author: Devansh Sanghavi
